choices.text: Name {ot4_b}, and have the roll rewritten in one column

choices.text: Let the two columns stand another season

effects.log: The columns stand. The northern shrines, hearing of it, begin sending their gifts in two parcels.

events.text: Your sacred crane, which has perched on the Gate Shrine for three hundred years, now stands on one leg between the places of {npc} and {ot4_b} at every offering and will not choose. {ot4_voice} take it for an omen. {ot4_holder} says cranes are simply like that. choices.text: Say the crane has chosen {ot4_b}, and be glad of it

choices.text: Feed the crane and tell it nothing

choices.text: Lay a third bowl, empty, between them

effects.log: The third bowl stays through the week. The lesser gods debate its meaning and none of the answers is yours.

events.text: The two sides of the domain have begun to keep different hours of prayer. {npc}'s shrines ring the dawn bell a quarter-hour early, and {ot4_b}'s answer by ringing theirs late. Pilgrims at the crossing do not know which to obey. A child offers a coin to whichever bell is right, and both bells are rung louder.

choices.text: Side with {npc}'s hour, and say so at the crossing

effects.log: The crossing hears it. {ot4_b}'s bell is not rung the next dawn, and the silence is worse than the noise.

choices.text: Side with {ot4_b}'s hour, and say so at the crossing

effects.log: The crossing hears it. {npc}'s bell is not rung the next dawn, and the silence is worse than the noise.

choices.text: Set a third bell, ringing exactly between the two

effects.log: The new bell rings at the middle hour. Both parties scorn it, and both obey it.

choices.text: Leave the bells and tell the pilgrims to follow the sun

effects.log: The pilgrims do, and go on stopping at both altars for good measure.

events.text: At the autumn procession the two parties carry the same image of the founding god, and have both brought litters. The image is split between them for the first mile, then reassembled at the bridge by a lesser god of bridges, who has had enough. The faithful line the road, and talk of nothing else.

choices.text: Take {npc}'s litter, and walk beside it

effects.log: You walk the long road at {npc}'s side. {ot4_b}'s litter trails behind you, and does not catch up.

choices.text: Take {ot4_b}'s litter, and walk beside it

effects.log: You walk the long road at {ot4_b}'s side. {npc}'s litter trails behind you, and does not catch up.

choices.text: Carry the image yourself, with no litter

effects.log: The image is lighter than you feared. The faithful sing, and the two parties walk in step at last, one pace behind.

choices.text: Watch from the bridge with the lesser god

effects.log: The god of bridges gives you tea and the dry opinion that all processions end in the same place. You watch them end.

events.text: The young gods of your temples play a ball game in the court each festival, and this year the teams have been drawn, without comment, by allegiance. The game is rough. A broken lamp and a torn banner later, the lesser gods ask whether the referee ought to be you. The ball waits in the dust.

choices.text: Referee, and rule for {ot4_b}'s side on every doubtful call

effects.log: Your calls are heard and read. The game ends in a quarrel instead of a draw, and {npc} congratulates {ot4_b} through gritted teeth.

choices.text: Referee fairly, and make both sides share the cake after

effects.log: The game is dull and the cake is good. Under the cake, a little of the heat goes out of the court.

effects.log: The porter blows it once, mildly, and the game dissolves into laughter. It is the first laughter in the court for a month.

events.text: Offerings of grain, sealed for the autumn feast, arrive at the storehouse of the domain and are found to be half sand. Someone swapped them in the night. The clerks name three suspects, and the third is a cousin of {npc}. The first two are of {ot4_b}'s following. Everyone is quick to say it is not about the succession.

choices.text: Clear {npc}'s cousin and press on the other two

choices.text: Clear the two of {ot4_b}'s following and press on the cousin

effects.log: The two are cleared. The cousin is summoned. {npc} comes in person, white to the lips.

choices.text: Order the whole storehouse swept and weighed again

effects.log: The weighing takes four days. Nine other thefts come to light, none of them about the throne, which is its own comfort.

choices.text: Hold all three until the feast, and feed them well

effects.log: They are fed and kept, and quietly miserable. By the feast it is plain none of them knew.

effects.log: {npc} unrolls it, reads it in the lamplight, and folds it into the register. The first page of the new domain is written in your hand.

events.text: The last evening before the parting, {npc} walks the cloisters alone, touching each pillar in passing. The lesser gods of both parties are in their cells. The temple is more silent than at any festival. At the end of the gallery {He} stops at the shrine of the founding god, lights a single stick, and does not pray aloud.

choices.text: Join {him} at the founding god's shrine and light a stick of your own

effects.log: The two sticks burn side by side. Neither of you says a word. The smoke mingles near the roof.

choices.text: Leave a lamp lit on the gallery for {him} to find on the way out

effects.log: The lamp burns until dawn. In the morning {npc} blows it out, and takes its oil in a small flask.

events.text: A cloud-clerk of the Court of Registers comes to your door with a wax tablet, and tells you that {b8oh_house} has been entered in the roll of lawful cults under your name. The entry is small. The clerk's thumb leaves a smear in the corner, and the clerk apologises for it, twice, to a god who has not noticed.

choices.text: Ask how much a cult weighs on the roll

effects.log: "A feather," says the clerk. "Until it is a stone." You carry the answer with you all day.

choices.text: Press the smeared corner flat with your own thumb

effects.log: The smear dries under your thumb into a small mark. The clerk watches it with the face of a man who has seen a seal made.

events.text: At the dawn bell, a child of a mortal village leaves a handful of millet before the altar of {b8oh_house} and says, to the air, that her father is ill. She does not know there is a god in the room. The offering is small, and heavier than the palace gates of your old life.

choices.text: Hear the prayer, and let it stay unanswered for now

effects.log: You listen to the whole of it. She leaves comforted by nothing but having said it, and you find you are comforted too.

choices.text: Follow her home along the cloud-thread

effects.log: A thread of smoke leads you to a low farmhouse. The father is asleep with a fever. The kettle on the hearth is already warm.

events.text: A gate-spirit with a cracked lantern drifts across the court of {b8oh_house} and asks whether the new god would care to name the doorposts. Nobody has named them in an age. The spirit holds out a slip of bamboo and a brush as if it were a small present.

choices.text: Name the doorposts yourself, one syllable each

effects.log: The spirit writes the syllables with great care. The doorposts hum a little, as wood does when it is addressed.

choices.text: Ask the spirit what they were called before

effects.log: "Nothing," says the spirit. "They have been waiting." The lantern brightens, just a little.

events.text: The Book of Fates is brought to your altar in a cedar case by two scribes in white, who open it to the page where {b8oh_house} stands, written in a hand that is yours and is not yours yet. A line of faith runs beneath the name, thin as thread, and each of the scribes finds a reason to look at the ceiling.

choices.text: Read your own line, and ask if it can be corrected

effects.log: "It is a draft," one scribe says kindly. "They are all drafts." You are not quite comforted.

choices.text: Offer the scribes tea of evening dew

effects.log: They drink, and a thaw comes over the room. The line beneath the name does not change, but it seems to settle.

events.text: A lesser god of kitchens, who has long served other altars, arrives at {b8oh_house} with a pot of bean paste on his hip and asks to be taken on. He says the old altars all smell of other gods. Yours smells, he says, of new rain. He sets the pot on the step and will not take it back.

choices.text: Take him on, and put the pot in the hall

effects.log: He is delighted. By dusk the court smells of fermenting beans and warm rice, and no prayer is the lonelier for it.

choices.text: Ask what he knows of the people who will come to pray

effects.log: He talks until the moon is high: who is grieving, who is proud, whose well has run dry. It is more than any scroll would tell you.

events.text: The first festival of {b8oh_house} draws three worshippers and a goat. One of the worshippers weeps; the other two are polite; the goat eats the garland. A priestess from a neighbouring cult drops by to see how it is going and stays to tie the garland back on, kindly, without a word.

choices.text: Thank the priestess, and ask her how she began

effects.log: "Alone, with a goat," she says, and laughs. You laugh as well, for the first time that month.

choices.text: Give the goat a name, and let it stay

effects.log: The goat answers to the name by the next morning, or so the worshippers swear. A small cult is made of such oaths.

events.text: In the Hall of Hours the lamps for your ten altars are lit in a row, and the eleventh stands dark by the wall with the name of {b8oh_house} on its base. The keeper of the lamps looks from one row to the other. "A god may carry ten," the keeper says. "No one has asked what happens to the eleventh."

choices.text: Leave {b8oh_house} unlit

effects.log: The keeper nods and takes the dark lamp away on a tray. It is carried out gently, like a sleeping child.

choices.text: Put out the dimmest of the ten, and light the eleventh

effects.log: The dimmest lamp is pinched out between two fingers. Somewhere a small hearth cools, and the keeper writes it down without comment.

events.text: A herald of the Court of Registers weighs you on a pair of brass scales and finds you a little over. "You carry ten and a half already," he says, "and {b8oh_founder} on the roll of {b8oh_house} would be the next half." He tilts the scale as he speaks, so you can see it, and waits for you to choose.

choices.text: Withdraw your name from the roll of {b8oh_house}

effects.log: The herald strikes it out in a clean line. The scale rights itself, and the cult goes on without you, as it did before.

choices.text: Release the faintest of your ten, and keep the new one

effects.log: The herald frowns, then writes it. The faintest of the ten sighs once, and is quiet.

choices.text: Ask the herald to hold the scale until the next moon

effects.log: He sighs, but holds. The scale quivers in his hand as though it, too, would like to know.

events.text: In the night every altar you keep gives a small knock, like a neighbour at a wall. The keeper of the roll comes before dawn to explain, in a whisper, that the eleventh altar, {b8oh_house}, cannot be lit without something going dark. "The sky is only so wide," the keeper says, and dabs a tear.

choices.text: Step back, and let {b8oh_house} go on without you

effects.log: You step back. The knocking stops. The keeper bows, and the cult is left to the gods who will tend it.

choices.text: Dim your least-visited altar, and take on the new one

effects.log: The least-visited altar is dimmed, and a sad clerk crosses its name off the list. The new altar lights, warm.

events.text: A petitioner from {b8oh_house}, an old widow with a bundle of reeds, tries to leave her offering at your altar and finds the offering returned to her hand by the weight of the roll. You see her face. The herald of the Court says the rule is the rule. "Choose," he says. "She waits."

choices.text: Send the offering back with a kind word

effects.log: The widow takes it with a bow, and goes. The roll accepts your choice without ceremony.

choices.text: Let the faintest of your ten fall silent, and take her offering

effects.log: The widow's offering is taken. Somewhere a small prayer stops, and the herald makes a mark.

choices.text: Ask the herald to postpone the choice by a night

effects.log: The herald checks his tablets and grudgingly allows it. The widow sits down to wait on the step.

events.text: A scrap of paper, folded small, drifts into your sleeve on the cloud-road. It is a prayer from a mortal keeper of {b8oh_house}: the dew has fouled the offering-bowls, and the dye of the banners has run. The hand is that of a very old person. The name at the head is {b8oh_founder}, written with the care of people who write it daily.

choices.text: Follow the paper down to the banner-hall

effects.log: The banner-hall is small and tidy. The dye has indeed run. A keeper looks up from a vat, and does not know who has come.

choices.text: Pass the paper on to the Court of Dyers

effects.log: The Court of Dyers takes it with thanks. You feel the paper's absence in your sleeve for the rest of the day.

events.text: At the divine exchange, two minor gods at a table are comparing their cults, and one praises the quiet of {b8oh_house}. "{b8oh_gens} keepers, and they still brew the founding tea by the same recipe," he says. Your mouth tastes of that tea, though you have never lifted the cup.

choices.text: Ask where the tea is brewed

effects.log: He tells you, kindly, and sells you a pinch of the leaf. It tastes of home you have never had.

choices.text: Buy a cup of the exchange's plain tea, and listen on

effects.log: They go on about the cult for an hour. By the end you know the names of the keepers, and not one of them is a stranger.

events.text: A janitor of the Book of Fates, sweeping the stacks, slides a thin volume across the desk to you without being asked. It is a register of cults. A page is marked: {b8oh_house}, {b8oh_gens} keepers, {b8oh_step}. In the margin, in a hand you almost recognise, someone has inked the word: patient.

choices.text: Copy the page into your sleeve, and the road with it

effects.log: You copy it. The janitor says nothing and goes on sweeping, with great attention to the corner by the window.

choices.text: Put the volume back, and ask the janitor about the margin

effects.log: "Old clerks leave notes," says the janitor. "Some mean something." He does not say which this is.

events.text: A goddess of orchards, at the feast of the Baekun pantheon, says that she keeps a stall at the gate of {b8oh_house} each autumn. "A tiny cult. {b8oh_step}. But the keepers pay in persimmons, and say a prayer for me by name." She looks at you for a long moment. "They have a way of saying yours, too."

choices.text: Say you would like to taste the persimmons

effects.log: She laughs and gives you one from her sleeve. It is sweet, and cold, and for a moment you smell a hearth.

choices.text: Ask her to take you to her stall at the gate

effects.log: She leads you down the cloud-road, chattering. At the gate a lamp is already lit, and the persimmons are laid out in rows.

events.text: A wind-courier drops a bundle on the steps of your hall: a prayer-roll from {b8oh_house}, with a mortal's thumbprint in the corner and a stain that might be tea. The roll asks for mercy on the winter stores. It addresses {b8oh_founder} without a title, as a neighbour might.

choices.text: Go and see the stores for yourself

effects.log: The stores are low but not hopeless. The keepers, who do not know you, offer you tea and a corner by the fire.

choices.text: Pass the roll to the Granary of Gods, and ask them to be generous

effects.log: The Granary takes the roll and nods. A letter comes back in a month, signed by a clerk with ink on both hands.

events.text: A bard of the lower cloud-roads sings a song of the south quarter in which a cult is named: {b8oh_house}, {b8oh_gens} keepers, a sweet bell, a lame porter. You know the lame porter's name before the bard sings it. The bard stops, stares, and finishes the verse in a lower voice.

choices.text: Ask the bard where she learned it

effects.log: She learned it from a grandmother who lived near the bell. You tip her, and she does not understand why.

choices.text: Buy the song, and keep it for the nights

effects.log: The song is cheap and the bard is glad. You hum it afterward without meaning to, and the porter's name comes to your tongue.

events.text: In the registry of lesser shrines, a clerk who has never met you mentions with a sigh that {b8oh_house} is {b8oh_step}, and that no one has applied for a grant on its behalf in years. "Proud people," the clerk says. "The sort who would rather mend a roof than ask." Her pen taps a small beat on the desk.

choices.text: Ask her to write you down the way to the shrine

effects.log: She writes a short, plain route, then adds a small drawing of a persimmon tree. "For the gate," she says.

choices.text: Ask what a grant would cost the Court

effects.log: She names a small figure. It is not much, and it is not nothing. You carry the number with you out of the registry.

events.text: Over a plate of rice cakes in the refectory of the Hwarin pantheon a young god whispers that he was born at the altar of {b8oh_house}, and that his first prayer was addressed to {b8oh_founder}. "I have asked my elders about the name," he says, "and they only smile." He asks if you have heard it.

choices.text: Say you have heard it, and leave it at that

effects.log: He looks at you a little too long and then lets it go. The rice cakes are good.

choices.text: Ask him to take you to the altar some day

effects.log: His face opens like a window. "I would be proud," he says, and means it.

events.text: At the gate of {b8oh_house} a young keeper is polishing the lintel, and does not stop as you approach. "You may go in," the keeper says, "it is the day of the open hall." On the lintel is carved the name {b8oh_founder}, worn by many fingers, and the keeper's cloth moves around it with a kind of respect.

choices.text: Go in, and take a seat among the visitors

effects.log: You sit. The visitors eat rice and plum wine and murmur. Nobody asks you anything, and nothing is missing.

choices.text: Lay a hand on the carved name

effects.log: The stone is warm. The young keeper stops polishing and watches your hand with a stillness that seems to be a prayer.

choices.text: Leave a sprig of pine on the sill and go

effects.log: A sprig of pine has been left on the sill each year, the keeper says to the air. You are not the first.

events.text: The offering day at {b8oh_house} brings seven hundred pilgrims, and you go up the steps with them in a plain robe. At the first altar the keepers recite the founding aloud. The name {b8oh_founder} is said without any weight, as one says the name of the weather. A child asks her mother whether the founder was a god or a man.

choices.text: Stand with the pilgrims, and eat their rice

effects.log: The pilgrims make room without looking at you. The rice is plain and hot and you find you are hungry.

choices.text: Tell the child the founder was both, and neither

effects.log: The child's mother stiffens, then softens. The child nods as if it were the clearest thing she had ever heard.

choices.text: Bow with the others and go out by the lesser gate

effects.log: You bow, and go out by the lesser gate, and are for a moment lighter than the wind.

events.text: Rain on the gate-roof of {b8oh_house}. A doorkeeper in a straw cloak is shelling beans under the eave, and without looking up says, "The first name-stone hums in the rain. It does it only for one kind of visitor." He cracks a pod. "I have never told a visitor that before. I am telling you because of the way you stand."

choices.text: Sit by him and shell beans until the rain lifts

effects.log: You shell beans. He tells you a long, rambling story about the temple cat. You do not say who you are, and he does not ask.

choices.text: Walk to the name-stone and let it hum

effects.log: The stone hums low and long. The doorkeeper puts down his bowl and bows his head, as if at a long-awaited visitor.

choices.text: Thank him for the tale and go on before the rain stops

effects.log: You walk on in the rain. A hum follows you down the road, quieter, and does not leave until the dawn.

events.text: On the great stair of {b8oh_house} a group of young keepers practise a welcome chant in the wrong key. The senior keeper corrects them, patiently, and tells them the old verse mentions a founder, {b8oh_founder}, who will one day return. The youngest looks at you, and then very hard at his shoes.

choices.text: Join the chant, softly, in the right key

effects.log: Your voice finds the true key and the young keepers, gaining courage, rise to it. The senior keeper closes her eyes.

choices.text: Tell them the founder would have liked the wrong key

effects.log: A ripple of laughter passes. The youngest keeper looks up, uncertain whether to believe you, and begins to smile.

choices.text: Nod to them, and slip out by the side stair

effects.log: You slip out. The chant behind you has found its key by the third verse.

events.text: A kitten sleeps on the cushion beside the first name-stone of {b8oh_house}, and a keeper brings tea for two without being asked. The stone reads {b8oh_founder}. The keeper says that this is the favourite seat of the temple cat, and also, by old custom, of any guest who comes without a name.

choices.text: Sit beside the kitten and take the tea

effects.log: The kitten stretches, shifts, and sleeps on. The tea is bitter and good, and it is the stillest hour you have had in an age.

choices.text: Rest your palm on the stone and say the name softly

effects.log: The stone is warm. The kitten wakes, looks at you, and goes back to sleep with the air of a creature whose suspicions are satisfied.

choices.text: Leave a coin of favour in the offering box and go

effects.log: The box takes the coin with a polite clink. The keeper, passing, murmurs a blessing so low you may have imagined it.

events.text: On the day of the pilgrim's lantern, {b8oh_house} lights a thousand paper lamps and floats them down the water-steps. Every keeper writes a name on a lamp. A new keeper, no older than twelve, holds out a blank lamp and a brush, and says that the lamp for {b8oh_founder} is always blank, in case.

choices.text: Take a lamp and join the keepers on the steps

effects.log: You launch the lamp with the rest. It drifts away in the dark, warm in the pool of its own light.

choices.text: Write the founder's name on the blank lamp

effects.log: The brush moves in your own hand, easily. The lamp floats out on the dark water, and no one on the steps says a word.

choices.text: Tell the boy the blank lamp is a fine custom, and keep walking

effects.log: The boy beams. You walk on past the steps, with the light of the thousand lamps on your sleeve.

events.text: Mist drifts through the gate of {b8oh_house} at the hour of the offering-gong, and the gong, half-struck, does not ring. The doorkeeper rubs his eyes. "The founder's name is on the lintel," he says to the mist, as one says a thing for one's own comfort. "I mean no harm in saying it. I like to say it."

choices.text: Ask him to let you listen to the quiet with him

effects.log: You sit on the step. The mist thickens. The gong sounds at last, soft as a breath, and the doorkeeper smiles.

choices.text: Say the name along with him

effects.log: He glances sideways, startled, then says it again, and your voices join. The mist parts as if drawn on a string.

choices.text: Slip through the gate while he is speaking

effects.log: You pass through and into the court. A lamp is lit for you by no hand you can see.

events.text: In the herb garden of {b8oh_house}, a keeper of great age is labelling jars. One jar is marked with a character you know, and under it, in a trembling hand: for the founder, when they come. The keeper does not look up. "Whoever you are," she says, "the kettle is warm."

choices.text: Sit down, and drink what is in the jar

effects.log: It is a tisane of mint and pear. It tastes like being told that someone has been waiting up for you.

choices.text: Read the label aloud, and say it is yours

effects.log: She closes her eyes and nods, once. "I knew it," she says quietly. "I did not think I would be right."

choices.text: Thank her for the kettle, and take the long way out

effects.log: You take the garden path. The jar stays on the shelf, with its label, waiting.

events.text: The keepers of {b8oh_house} have a game: they ask visitors to name the founder's favourite hymn. A visitor who guesses wrong pays a forfeit of a kiss on the cat's nose. The head-keeper looks at you with a gleam. "A new face! Perhaps the founder's own successor. Come, come, which hymn?"

choices.text: Pick the first hymn that comes to mind, and kiss the cat

effects.log: The cat accepts with dignity. The hall roars. You have been teased, and welcomed, in one breath.

choices.text: Say it is an ill game to play with a founder's name

effects.log: The laughter stops. The head-keeper sets the cat down and a lamp goes out by the door, softly, as a mark of displeasure.

choices.text: Ask if you may hear the hymn they think it was

effects.log: They sing it. It is a nursery song, wrong in every line. You listen to the end and nod as if it were rare.

events.text: At the midday meal, the novices of {b8oh_house} have put a straw crown on the founder's empty chair and are bowing to it with exaggerated solemnity. It is a joke older than any of them. A fresh-faced godling turns to you and invites you to take a bow for the founder, since you look the part.

choices.text: Bow to the chair, with a flourish of your own

effects.log: The novices applaud. The crown slips. Somebody pours you tea, and the joke is made over into a welcome.

choices.text: Remove the crown and set it aside

effects.log: The room stills. The head-keeper nods slowly. The novices are not shamed, but they are quiet through the meal.

events.text: A visiting priest of a rival cult makes a speech at the gate of {b8oh_house}. "A founder returned!" he cries, "and with hair as dry as a hearth-broom!" The crowd titters. The head-keeper, mortified, tries to hush him. You are, for a moment, the best entertainment in the south quarter.

choices.text: Smile along, and offer the priest a seat at the table

effects.log: He is nonplussed to be taken up. He sits. The cult's keepers breathe again, and the tension goes out of the court.

choices.text: Say the rival's cult will be remembered for its manners

effects.log: The priest flushes. The keepers murmur. A few of them will not meet your eye for a week.

choices.text: Ask the priest the name of the founder of his own cult

effects.log: He tells you, stumbling. You nod gravely, as if it were the finest name in the sky.

events.text: Over rice wine at the pilgrim inn, two keepers of {b8oh_house} tell the story of the false founders: nine of them, in nine generations, each with a ring, a scar and a good reason. You are expected to laugh. The tenth, they say, will be the funniest yet, and they raise their cups to you before they have finished the sentence.

choices.text: Raise your cup, and laugh with them

effects.log: You laugh. They laugh. Somewhere inside the laughter, a small door is left unlatched.

choices.text: Say that a tenth false founder would be a poor jest

effects.log: The laughter dies. The inn is as silent as a shrine. They have the grace to be ashamed, and the sense to say nothing.

events.text: A card pinned to the notice-board of {b8oh_house} reads, in an elegant script: Founder wanted. Must be dead for six hundred years. Apply within. A keeper takes it down and apologises. "Novices," she says, "with brushes." She looks at you, and you at the card, and there is a pause in which many things could happen.

choices.text: Take the card, and pin it back upside down

effects.log: She laughs so hard she has to sit down. The hall, hearing, laughs with her.

choices.text: Say the cult has more to answer for than a joke

effects.log: The keeper's laughter dies. She takes the card and tears it, very slowly, and does not apologise again.

choices.text: Ask for the brush and add a line of your own

effects.log: You write: applicant has references. She reads it, and her mouth twitches, and she leaves the card on the board.

events.text: The senior keeper of {b8oh_house}, {b8oh_head}, takes you to the oldest altar and sets a small bowl of water on it. "Say the thing the founder said when the first bowl was filled," {b8oh_head} says. "We have only a rumour of it. If you know it, the water will answer." The surface is perfectly still.

choices.text: Say what comes first to your tongue

effects.log: The words come in an old cadence. The water shivers once, then smoothes, and rises a finger's breadth in the bowl.

choices.text: Say you do not remember, and are sorry

effects.log: The water does not move. {b8oh_head} lifts the bowl with a gentle nod. "A true answer fills it, too, in time," the keeper murmurs.

choices.text: Ask {b8oh_head} what the rumour says

effects.log: {b8oh_head} gives you a line, halting. It is nearly right, and wrong in a way only you would know.

events.text: Three bowls are set before you at the evening service of {b8oh_house}: wine, millet, and a spray of plum blossom. {b8oh_head} says the founder is said to have taken only the one the others had overlooked. The keepers watch, and some of them are surely holding their breath on the outcome.

choices.text: Pour the wine out for the keepers

effects.log: They are charmed. The wine, by its smell, is thin and sweet, and whatever was hoped for in the silence is paid in cheerful smiles.

choices.text: Take the millet, and share it with the nearest child

effects.log: The child eats with solemn pleasure. {b8oh_head} watches with an expression you cannot read.

choices.text: Take the blossom, and tuck it behind the altar-lamp

effects.log: The blossom opens a little in the lamplight. {b8oh_head} lets out a breath that might have been a laugh.

events.text: At the quarter-hour of the evening rite, {b8oh_head} of {b8oh_house} puts a question to you in front of the keepers: "When the founder left, which door of the hall was left unlatched?" Four doors, four lamps. A nervous cough runs through the room.

choices.text: Point to the one that feels right

effects.log: The door opens at a touch. The keepers do not cheer. They only lower their eyes in an old, grateful way.

choices.text: Say you do not know, and would not like to guess

effects.log: The head-keeper nods and puts the question away. "That, too, is a way of keeping a hall," is all the keeper says.

choices.text: Ask which door the keepers have always left open

effects.log: A younger keeper answers, flustered. {b8oh_head} smiles at the youngster, and then at you.

events.text: A scroll is unrolled for you in the library of {b8oh_house}, and {b8oh_head} asks you to say aloud the first verse. It is in an old script that no one living reads, and the keepers have kept it by shape alone. You are asked, not unkindly, to see if your tongue can do what their eyes cannot.

choices.text: Read the verse aloud, and let the old words fall

effects.log: The old words come, one after the other. The keepers sit very straight. One of them begins, quietly, to weep.

choices.text: Admit you can read only the shapes, not the words

effects.log: {b8oh_head} smiles. "Shapes are how the hall has always known you," the keeper says, and rolls the scroll back with great care.

choices.text: Offer to copy it out in a modern hand, for the young keepers

effects.log: {b8oh_head} gives you a brush. The copy takes the afternoon. The young keepers read it over your shoulder, and no one speaks.

events.text: On the tenth day of your stay at {b8oh_house}, {b8oh_head} hands you a plain cup and asks you to fill it from the old well, and to say which of the three buckets you took. There are buckets of ash, of birch and of iron, and a long tradition about which of them the founder always chose.

choices.text: Take the first bucket you see

effects.log: The cup fills sweet and cold. {b8oh_head} lets it be drunk without comment, which is a comment of its own.

choices.text: Take none, and drink from the well with your hands

effects.log: {b8oh_head} laughs aloud, and the keepers join. "That too is in the lore," the keeper says. "We forgot it."

choices.text: Ask {b8oh_head} which bucket they would have chosen

effects.log: "The iron," says {b8oh_head}. "Always. But I wish I had chosen the ash."

events.text: The oldest keeper of {b8oh_house} sets a small bell on the altar in front of you. "It rang when the founder left," the old one says, "and has never rung since. I have tried it every morning for sixty years." {b8oh_head}, beside the keeper, holds a breath that lasts a very long time.

choices.text: Lift the bell, and ring it once

effects.log: The bell rings, thin and sweet, across the hall. The old keeper kneels, and the others follow, one by one.

choices.text: Leave the bell where it lies, and ask for a season of tea and talk

effects.log: The old keeper nods. "We have waited this long," is all the answer. The bell stays on the altar, quiet, and somehow warmer.

events.text: In the winter hall of {b8oh_house}, a child in a quilted coat is made to recite a rhyme that has no source, and which {b8oh_head} says has been taught for six hundred years as a nursery song. Its third line is one you know. The child says it half a breath behind you. The room stills.

choices.text: Say the rhyme with the child, line for line

effects.log: The child's voice joins yours, and the keepers one by one take up the verse. It is a warmer sound than any hymn.

choices.text: Tell the child it was a fine rhyme, and leave it be

effects.log: The child grins, and goes back to the stove. The keepers watch you go. Nobody has been told, and everyone knows.

events.text: A pilgrim from the high pass of the Haeryong pantheon has walked four days to light a stick at {b8oh_house}. In the hall she kneels beside you, and without a glance says, "Forgive an old woman: the founder had your walk." {b8oh_head} hears this. The incense-bowl, at the altar, cracks with a faint, clean sound.

choices.text: Let the keepers think what they like, and light a stick

effects.log: The stick catches on the first match. The keepers begin, in whispers, to call you by an old title, and you do not stop them.

choices.text: Tell the pilgrim she may be mistaken, and gently

effects.log: She smiles and folds her hands. "Perhaps," she says. "Walks are strange." She does not look convinced.

events.text: The keepers of {b8oh_house} have kept the founder's lamp lit for six hundred years, and tonight the oil has failed. The lamp gutters, flares, and settles to a new colour, a soft gold none of them has seen. {b8oh_head} asks, as if it were a question about the weather, whether you will hold the wick for them.

choices.text: Hold the wick, and let it burn in your hand

effects.log: The wick burns steady, and the gold deepens. The keepers fall to their knees without a sound, and the lamp's oil is not mentioned again.

choices.text: Pour more oil into the lamp, and say it was only the oil

effects.log: The lamp returns to its old colour. {b8oh_head} thanks you with the tact of a long career, and does not quite believe you.

events.text: A letter in a very old hand has been tucked into the foundation-stone of {b8oh_house}, and it is opened this morning for the first time. It is addressed to a keeper who has not yet been born, and mentions, in its second line, a visitor with the exact mannerisms you have. {b8oh_head} reads it aloud, reddening, and holds the letter out.

choices.text: Take the letter, and read the next line aloud

effects.log: You read it, and the room hushes. It tells of a promise kept, and a promise to come. The keepers kneel.

choices.text: Fold the letter and give it back, unread, with thanks

effects.log: {b8oh_head} accepts it with open relief. The letter is put back in the stone, and the keepers go quietly to their breakfast.

events.text: After a year of sitting at the lower table of {b8oh_house}, you are asked, with bowls of tea and a quiet drumming of the gong, to take the rank of {b8oh_next}. A green-sashed godling stands at the end of the row, hoping not to be noticed, and clearly hoping the post will be hers.

choices.text: Accept the sash with gratitude

effects.log: The sash is cool and heavy. The keepers bow as you pass, and your seat in the hall is a little nearer the altar from that day.

choices.text: Pass the sash to the green-sashed godling

effects.log: She takes it with a gasp. {b8oh_head} writes the name with a slow hand, and tells no one how seldom this is done.

choices.text: Decline, and remain at the lower table

effects.log: You keep your old seat. The offer is withdrawn with a bow, and a few keepers, afterwards, bring you extra tea.

events.text: The keepers of {b8oh_house} gather on the longest night to elevate you to {b8oh_next}. The sash is woven of red cord, the same shade as the lamp-wick, and it has been kept in cedar for years. {b8oh_head} places it across your shoulders with the old formula, and a hush falls that is almost fear.

choices.text: Wear the sash, and speak the formula back

effects.log: The formula comes easily. The keepers bow as one, and the lamp-wick flares a warmer colour.

choices.text: Ask who wove the cord

effects.log: "A keeper long dead," says {b8oh_head}. "She wove it for someone she would never meet." The room is very quiet.

choices.text: Return the sash with thanks, and ask to earn it in time

effects.log: {b8oh_head} accepts the sash. "Earn, then," the old keeper says, almost fondly. The sash is folded back in its cedar.

events.text: The Book of Fates adds, without ceremony and in an unfamiliar hand, a line to the roll of {b8oh_house}: your name, and the rank of {b8oh_next}. The keepers read it at the evening service. The incense in the hall changes, subtly, to the blend that was only ever burned for the head's own guests.

choices.text: Accept the title, and take your new seat

effects.log: The seat is a little warmer than the old one. The keepers bring tea, and it is carried to you in both hands.

choices.text: Ask the Book to wait a season before the title is made final

effects.log: The Book, after a pause, strikes the line in pencil. The keepers murmur their approval. The wait is understood.

events.text: A drought has thinned the harvest of the villages around {b8oh_house}, and the keepers, in distress, ask you to stand as {b8oh_next} to lend the cult the weight of a higher name. A young godling of springs looks on, and in her face is a request she does not know how to make.

choices.text: Accept the rank, and speak for the villages

effects.log: The rank is yours. The villages, hearing, send what they can. The drought breaks in the third week, as droughts sometimes do.

choices.text: Step aside, and recommend the godling of springs for the rank

effects.log: The godling's eyes fill. {b8oh_head} nods. The villages send their offerings to her, and the cult is the better for it.

choices.text: Decline the rank, and lend a hand with the harvest instead

effects.log: You spend the dry weeks hauling water. The keepers do not forget who stood beside them.

events.text: At the festival of the third moon, the keepers of {b8oh_house} sing the elevation hymn. It has been sung for the last six heads, and for none in between. When the last verse ends, {b8oh_head} places a ribbon in your hand and tells you, kindly, that the post of {b8oh_next} is now open to you.

choices.text: Take the ribbon, and tie it to your sleeve

effects.log: The ribbon sits on your sleeve like a small bright moth. The keepers look at it fondly.

choices.text: Ask why the hymn was sung so seldom

effects.log: "Because the heads were few," says {b8oh_head}. "We are glad of you, and mean it." You tie the ribbon, more slowly.

choices.text: Return the ribbon, and ask for a year of quiet service first

effects.log: {b8oh_head} accepts, unoffended. "A year," the keeper says. "We have waited longer."

events.text: The scribes of the Book of Fates send word that the roll of {b8oh_house} now lists you as {b8oh_next}, whether or not the cult has asked. The keepers, wanting to avoid a fuss, have set a new cushion in the hall for you. A very small godling has been sent to sweep it.

choices.text: Take the cushion with thanks

effects.log: The cushion is thick and well-stuffed. You sit on it as if it had always been yours, and the little sweeper beams.

choices.text: Ask the Book to redraw the line, with a delay

effects.log: The Book considers, then pencils a faint question mark beside your name. The keepers take the cushion away, politely, to wait.

events.text: A cold wind has thinned the harvest of the villages around {b8oh_house}, and the autumn offerings are small. The keepers, with great tact, set the last of the plum wine before you, the {b8oh_rank}, and say nothing. The silence is thick and smells of cold rice.

choices.text: Help the keepers draw up a fairer roll of tithes

effects.log: You sit with the ledger through the long night. The roll is shorter and juster, and it is signed in the morning by every elder.

choices.text: Quietly set aside the best of the offerings for your own table

effects.log: The offerings are taken and not remarked on. The cult's winter is the leaner for it, and a keeper's face goes thin.

choices.text: Say it is not your place, and leave early

effects.log: The keepers see you to the gate with bows. You hear them, behind you, begin on the ledger without you.

events.text: The feast of the second harvest at {b8oh_house} seats the {b8oh_rank} beside a shy godling of ditches who has never dined with a Head. She holds her chopsticks as if they were holy relics, and whispers that she is not sure which cup is hers. The hall is watching, with a slow and loving cruelty.

choices.text: Quietly coach her through the meal

effects.log: She finishes the meal with colour in her cheeks. The elders watch, and one of them, unseen, nods approval.

choices.text: Let her fumble, and take amusement in the sight

effects.log: The meal ends in a knocked cup. She flees. The elders look at you and look away, and no one laughs.

choices.text: Excuse yourself before the second course

effects.log: You leave early. The godling's relief is audible. The cook sends your portion to your rooms, uncommented.

events.text: On the night of the lantern fast, {b8oh_house} must choose a verse for the closing hymn, and two elders disagree. A young keeper, the {b8oh_rank}'s newest friend, brings the dispute to you in a whisper. All eyes are on the scroll in your hand, which holds both verses.

choices.text: Recite the older verse from memory

effects.log: The old verse comes without a pause. The elders are silenced, and one is moved.

choices.text: Pick the shorter verse, because you are hungry

effects.log: The hall breaks into laughter, and the elders, scandalised, are silent. The shorter verse is sung. It is not forgiven.

choices.text: Say that a hymn is chosen by the throats that sing it

effects.log: The elders blink. The hall sings both, in a ragged, wonderful round. It is not the correct way, and it is the best hymn in years.

events.text: The cult-house of {b8oh_house} runs short of firewood in the last week of the year, and the keepers draw lots for who may sleep nearest the stove. The {b8oh_rank} is offered the first draw as a courtesy, and the room, as one, pretends not to be hoping for refusal.

choices.text: Give your draw to the oldest keeper, and shiver in her place

effects.log: She takes the warm place with a bow of thanks. You spend the night with a blanket and a conversation, which is warmer than it sounds.

choices.text: Take the offered place, with an easy air

effects.log: You sleep well. The keepers whisper in the morning. The firewood, somewhere, finds its way to the rest of the hall.

choices.text: Refuse the draw, and fetch firewood from the grove

effects.log: You return with a loaded sledge at midnight. The keepers cheer, softly, so as not to wake the sleepers.

events.text: A debt of oil is owed by {b8oh_house} to a trader god of the lower cloud-roads, and the keepers have no way to pay it before the new moon. They do not ask the {b8oh_rank} for help. They tidy the court, and sweep the stair, and look at you with the faces of children who are not asking.

choices.text: Write to the trader, and plead the case of the cult

effects.log: Your letter is courteous and plain. The trader, after a pause, accepts a delay. The keepers are quiet with relief.

choices.text: Quietly draw on the guest portion of the offerings to cover your own costs

effects.log: No one counts the guest portion. The debt remains, and the keepers go on sweeping a little more slowly.

choices.text: Say that you cannot stay for the settling of accounts

effects.log: You make your excuses. The keepers see you off with bows, and not a trace of reproach.

events.text: The oldest godling of ditches at {b8oh_house} refuses to be moved from her place at the head of the table, though she is deaf, half-blind and has lost her teeth. The {b8oh_rank} is asked, as a guest of weight, to say a word. The younger keepers wait, hoping for a diplomatic lie.

choices.text: Stay beside her, and coax her to the warmer seat

effects.log: She grumbles, then yields. You carry her bowl. It is humble work, and the keepers notice.

choices.text: Tell the younger keepers to stop fussing, and eat

effects.log: The younger keepers flush. The old godling, hearing nothing, chews on. The meal ends in a stiff silence.

choices.text: Say you have a long road tomorrow, and leave the table

effects.log: You leave. The old godling, behind you, calls for the soup as if nothing had happened.

events.text: The spring rite of {b8oh_house} has three versions of the closing blessing, and the elders have quarrelled over them for twenty years. Now they ask the {b8oh_rank} to choose, with the cheerful desperation of old friends who are very tired of arguing. A priest of the Hwarin pantheon, on a visit, listens with interest.

choices.text: Recite the blessing as it was said in the first days

effects.log: The words come right. The elders clap their hands, relieved and ashamed, and the old quarrel is finally put to bed.

choices.text: Choose the oddest version, as a jest

effects.log: The hall gasps, then laughs. The oddest version is sung, and does not offend a soul, and the quarrel, absurdly, ends.

choices.text: Say the blessing is the sort of thing that must be found, not given

effects.log: The elders murmur. The priest from Hwarin writes this down in his small book, and the quarrel goes on.

events.text: In the dead of winter, the roof of the south hall of {b8oh_house} sags under snow, and the keepers carry out their sleeping-mats to the main court. The {b8oh_rank} is offered a place under the only dry eave, and several of the keepers do not look at the eave at all.

choices.text: Give the dry place to the smallest godling, and sleep in the snow-light

effects.log: You sleep poorly and well. In the morning the keepers bring tea without saying why.

choices.text: Take the dry place without a word

effects.log: You sleep soundly. The smallest godling coughs in the night, and the keepers watch, and are patient.

choices.text: Excuse yourself, and walk down the cloud-road to find a warmer inn

effects.log: You find an inn. The keepers' mats are, by dawn, covered in frost, and they do not complain.

events.text: {b8oh_old_head} of {b8oh_house} is gone to the long dark, and the altar is silent. The keepers cannot agree on the succession: the able deputy {b8oh_head} stands at one pillar, and a younger kinsman, much loved, stands at another. All the eyes in the court turn to the {b8oh_rank}, who has been the cult's guest for a long season.

choices.text: Name {b8oh_head}, the deputy who has done the work

effects.log: The name is said, and the court breathes. The kinsman bows without bitterness, and the old head's lamp is lit anew.

choices.text: Name the kinsman, whom the keepers love

effects.log: The name is said, and the court sighs. {b8oh_head} bows with grace. The incense burns a little sweeter for the affection in it.

events.text: The lamps of {b8oh_house} gutter in the night as the old head, {b8oh_old_head}, passes. At dawn the elders find the roll of succession blank, since the old head died without writing it. They ask the {b8oh_rank}, in the hushed, faltering voice of people who are afraid of the answer, to say the name.

choices.text: Say the name of {b8oh_head}, who kept the cult through the lean years

effects.log: The elders write it with slow hands. The cult wakes to a head who has earned the post and knows the cost.

choices.text: Say the name of the old head's kin, so the house stays unbroken

effects.log: The elders write it with tears. The cult wakes to an unproven head, whom everyone is determined to love.

events.text: At the funeral of {b8oh_old_head}, the keepers of {b8oh_house} sit in two rows and say nothing to each other. In the middle of the service a runner from the Court of Registers delivers a sealed question: who shall be the next head? The {b8oh_rank} is asked to sign the answer.

choices.text: Sign for {b8oh_head}, the deputy

effects.log: The pen scratches. The runner takes the reply and goes. {b8oh_head} stands very straight, shaking.

choices.text: Sign for the old head's kinsman

effects.log: The pen scratches. The runner takes the reply and goes. The kinsman covers his face with his sleeve.

events.text: Two letters arrive at the gate of {b8oh_house} on the same morning: one from the able deputy {b8oh_head}, asking, with a dignity that costs, for the headship; the other from the old head's kinsman, asking nothing, and thanking the {b8oh_rank} for years of kindness. The mud of the road is still on both seals.

choices.text: Reply to {b8oh_head} with your support

effects.log: Your reply goes out by the evening wind. The kinsman, learning, writes you a very correct note of thanks, and visits the cult no more.

choices.text: Reply to the kinsman, and ask him to stay

effects.log: Your reply goes out. {b8oh_head} reads it in the stable, alone, and later folds it into a sleeve with a steady hand.

events.text: A cold rain falls on the burial of {b8oh_old_head}. The keepers of {b8oh_house} huddle under the eaves, and the question of the headship rises like steam. The deputy {b8oh_head} is cleverer, the kinsman kinder. The {b8oh_rank} has been guest at the table for years and is asked, in a murmur, to decide.

choices.text: Stand beside {b8oh_head} under the eave

effects.log: You stand. The rain softens. The keepers shuffle closer to the deputy, and the matter is settled in that silent shuffle.

choices.text: Stand beside the kinsman, and offer him your cloak

effects.log: You stand. The keepers shuffle closer to the kinsman, and the matter is settled in that silent shuffle.

events.text: A swallow brings word, tied under its wing, that {b8oh_house} is {b8oh_step}. The cold has split the altar-stone, the bell-rope is frayed, and the old porter has sold his only cloak to pay for incense. The note ends: "We do not ask. We tell you only so you will know."

choices.text: Send a gift of faith by the same swallow: {b8oh_help}

effects.log: The swallow is gone before you finish writing. Its return, days later, brings only a single feather and a thank-you.

choices.text: Fold the note away, and let it be

effects.log: You fold the note into your sleeve. It sits there for a long time, light as a leaf.

events.text: A carrier of the Hall of Letters, wet and breathless, mentions as she hands you your post that {b8oh_house} is {b8oh_step}, and that the keepers have taken to praying in the lane because the hall is cold. She says it as one says a thing in passing. She has been walking a long road to say it.

choices.text: Send help by the carrier's own hand: {b8oh_help}

effects.log: The carrier takes the gift with a nod. Weeks later, a drawing of the repaired roof comes back, done in a child's hand.

choices.text: Thank the carrier, and let the news settle

effects.log: The carrier goes, and the news settles in you like silt. You think of it at odd hours.

events.text: A crow lands on your window-sill with a scrap of cloth tied to its leg. The cloth is a keeper's sash, torn, and a short note says {b8oh_house} is {b8oh_step}. The keepers, it says, have not forgotten. The crow, which has a long road behind it, accepts a crumb of rice and does not leave.

choices.text: Send a gift of faith back with the crow: {b8oh_help}

effects.log: The crow takes the parcel in its beak, with a sour look, and goes. The parcel arrives intact, or so the note says.

choices.text: Feed the crow, and say nothing

effects.log: The crow eats, and watches you with an old, shrewd eye. It leaves at dusk with an air of reproach.

events.text: The wind through your hall brings a whisper from the south quarter: {b8oh_house} is {b8oh_step}, and the keepers have begun to sell the temple's lesser bells. A pilgrim, passing, says she has heard it sing in a stranger's house. She says it without malice, and without knowing whose name is at the top of the cult's roll.

choices.text: Send help quietly: {b8oh_help}

effects.log: The help goes by the wind, and the bells, a season later, are said to ring again.

choices.text: Let the news pass over you, like weather

effects.log: You let it pass. It does not entirely leave.

events.text: A merchant-god from the southern ports remarks at your table that {b8oh_house} is {b8oh_step}. He says it neutrally, as a merchant might. Then he adds that the keepers still hang a lantern in the east window each night, for a founder who has not returned, and that he finds the custom strange.

choices.text: Send help by the merchant's own ships: {b8oh_help}

effects.log: The merchant takes the commission with a flick of the wrist. A lantern, in the east window, burns a little brighter that winter.

choices.text: Ask the merchant to tell you more of the lantern

effects.log: He tells you what he knows, which is not much. The lantern is lit at the hour you used to wake.

events.text: A clerk of the Court of Registers sends, in the course of routine correspondence, a notice that {b8oh_house} has applied for relief and been refused for want of a sponsor. The relief is {b8oh_step} in kind. The clerk adds, in a small hand at the bottom: I thought you might wish to know.

choices.text: Sponsor the cult, and send help: {b8oh_help}

effects.log: The clerk's reply is a single stamp. The cult is entered on the roll of relief, and no one writes to say so.

choices.text: File the notice, and let the Court's decision stand

effects.log: You file it. The clerk's small hand at the bottom is not forgotten.

events.text: The bell of the dying altars tolls three times at dawn, and a lesser god of messages whispers the name: {b8oh_house}. It is no more. The last keeper, an old woman, put out the final lamp and walked down the cloud-road. You stand a long time with a stick of incense in your hand, and do not light it.

choices.text: Say the founder's name once, and let the wind take it

effects.log: You say it, and the wind lifts it from your lips. Nothing answers, and nothing needs to.

choices.text: Look south across the clouds until the light changes

effects.log: The light changes. The south quarter is as it always was, a stretch of cloud, and now it has a gap in it you can feel.

events.text: Word comes by the evening rice-seller: {b8oh_house} has fallen, and its shrine is a heap of timber. The seller has no particular grief; she only mentions that the persimmon tree at the gate still stood, and that one child was seen carrying a branch of it away. You thank her and eat your rice.

choices.text: Light one stick of the old blend, and watch it burn

effects.log: The stick burns with the smell of a hearth you cannot place. When it is ash, you find your eyes are damp.

choices.text: Say nothing, and take a branch of persimmon from the market

effects.log: The persimmon is hard, and then ripe, and then gone. You keep the pit in a drawer without knowing why.

events.text: The Book of Fates turns a page without a sound, and the entry for {b8oh_house} is closed with a thin red line. A clerk reads it aloud at the evening reckoning. The last keepers have scattered. The gate-spirit has found a new gate. Your name, on the line above, is dry, and will stay so.

choices.text: Say the founder's name softly, to yourself

effects.log: The name rises in the cold air, and the lamp beside you gutters. You hold your hands over the flame to keep it.

choices.text: Ask the clerk to read the entry again, more slowly

effects.log: She reads it again. It is the same. This time you write down every word.

events.text: A pilgrim stops at your door on her way out of the world and tells you, between sips of tea, that {b8oh_house} is dust. She was a keeper there, the last but one. She says she does not blame the founder for being away. She says only that she kept the lamp lit as long as she could.

choices.text: Light a stick for the lamp, and thank her

effects.log: She watches the smoke rise, and bows. She goes, in the morning, with the look of someone who has put down a stone.

choices.text: Pour her a second cup, and listen to the rest

effects.log: She tells you the rest, which is long and plain and made of small kindnesses. You listen to every word.

events.text: In the shade of a prayer-wheel a ferryman-god sells charms and tells tales for the price of a bowl of barley. Today it is {llg_who}, who lived {llg_told_age} and left {llg_thing} in {llg_region}. "My aunt kept its lamps," he says, pausing to mend a net, "and she never said a kind word about anyone but this." Your tea cools in your hand.

choices.text: Ask the ferryman where the lamps are kept now

effects.log: He points with a netting needle, and tells you at length. You walk away with a direction and a lightness.

choices.text: Buy a charm, and say nothing

effects.log: The charm is a knot of red thread. It sits in your pocket like a small, warm stone for the rest of the week.

events.text: A scroll-seller at the pilgrim crossroads unrolls a map of high places for the season, and one is newly added: {llg_thing}, in {llg_region}, named for {llg_who}. She says {llg_he} died of {llg_cause}, or so the guide-book claims, and offers to copy it out. The name sits in your throat like a seed.

choices.text: Ask her what the guide-book says of the place

effects.log: She reads aloud. It is half wrong, and half so exact it makes your scalp prickle. You buy the copy.

choices.text: Trace the name in the dust of the cart with your finger

effects.log: The dust takes the shape as if it knew the stroke. The scroll-seller glances at it and, tactfully, looks away.

events.text: In a courtyard of the war-gods an instructor with a twisted wrist is teaching the stances of {llg_thing} in {llg_region}, which he says came down in an unbroken line from {llg_who}, {llg_years} years since. "Feet apart, like roots," he calls. Your feet, in the shade of the wall, have already found the spot.

choices.text: Join the back row and try the stance

effects.log: The stance fits you as a hand fits a glove. The instructor squints, and corrects the pupil beside you instead of you.

choices.text: Watch from the wall and keep your own counsel

effects.log: You watch the whole drill. A faint ache runs through your heels. The ache is almost fond.

events.text: A processional ballad, "{llg_song}," has taken the lower cloud-roads by storm, and the chorus runs: "{llg_verse}." It sings of {llg_who}, gone at {llg_told_age} of {llg_cause}, so the singer insists. You have never heard it. Yet each verse, a moment before the singer, forms in your mouth, and she gets it wrong, and you wince.

choices.text: Hum the right line under her breath

effects.log: She falters, glances sideways, and then sings your line, as if it had always been there.

choices.text: Drop a coin in her bowl and move on, quickly

effects.log: The coin rings in the bowl. The ballad follows you down two streets, and you do not sing along.

events.text: In {llg_region} every household sets a cup of tea on the doorstep at dusk, and has for {llg_years} years. A little girl, asked why, shrugs: "It is how the day closes." Nobody knows who began it. You watch a woman lay down her cup and lift her palm to her chest, and your own palm rises, without leave.

choices.text: Ask the girl to show you how the cup is laid

effects.log: She shows you with grave pride. Your hands, laying the cup, make the same small turn as hers, and neither of you remarks on it.

choices.text: Lower your hand and walk on, thinking of supper

effects.log: You walk on. A cup of tea steams behind you on the step, and you carry the smell for a long while.

events.text: Nobody in {llg_region} says the name {llg_who} after the evening bell. A grey-bearded river-god will, if paid double, and with a hand cupped to his mouth: how {llg_he} bound the shrines, how {llg_thing} was shuttered, and why it has stayed shut for {llg_years} years. He finishes, and nobody speaks. You find your throat is dry.

choices.text: Ask him what {llg_he} did to be so feared

effects.log: He tells you what he knows. It is less than the fear, and worse for being small.

choices.text: Say it was a long time ago, and pay him

effects.log: He nods, takes the coin, and says the answer is yes, of course, a long time. Neither of you believes it.

events.text: The tale of {llg_who} told by the war-gods is a dry thing, all sting and no thunder: where {llg_he} trained pupils, what became of those who failed, and why the yard at {llg_thing} is swept each dawn by a keeper who will not say who pays. The younger gods tell it in whispers. The old ones do not tell it at all.

choices.text: Ask the old keeper who still remembers the pupils

effects.log: The keeper looks at you a long time, then names three. All of them are gone. You write the names on your sleeve with your thumb.

choices.text: Say that you are expected elsewhere, and go

effects.log: You go. The yard at {llg_thing} stays at the edge of your mind until nightfall.

events.text: Each year the temple school of {llg_region} chants the register entry of {llg_who} from memory: dates, a given age of {llg_age}, a cause, {llg_cause}, and the seal of the Court. It is the dullest rite in the sky. Behind the wall a ferryman's gourd rattles out a rude tune. Someone, you decide, worked very hard to make this entry boring.

choices.text: Sit out the whole chant, and the silence after

effects.log: The chant ends. In the silence a swallow flies through the hall. You remember, absurdly, the swallow.

choices.text: Slip out to the gourd, and listen to the rude tune

effects.log: The tune is vulgar and cheerful. You laugh once, abruptly, in the lane.

events.text: A cloud-boat of pilgrims passes the dock with a leaking hold, bound for {llg_region} to see {llg_thing}. You hold the plank as they patch it. A grandmother among them pats the seat beside her. "You have the look of one who is going anyway," she says. "It is only a few seasons."

choices.text: Step aboard

effects.log: The boat takes your weight with a creak. The grandmother passes you a rice ball and a map.

choices.text: Wave them off from the dock

effects.log: They wave back. The boat dwindles into the grey, and you stay, with the leaving in your chest.

events.text: A steward of the Heavenly Court needs a sealed scroll delivered to {llg_region}, with a modest honorarium and no questions. You are about to say no when it dawns on you that you had meant to go there all along, ever since you first heard the name {llg_thing}, and have been quietly setting the days aside.

choices.text: Take the scroll

effects.log: The steward stamps the receipt and thanks you, with an air of one who expected the answer.

choices.text: Recommend another courier, and watch the steward go

effects.log: The steward does not argue. You are left with the odd sense of having refused a door that will open again.

events.text: A temple of your own domain stands in {llg_region}: {llg_Thing}, raised in the name of {llg_who}. The pilgrims come up its steps in their holiday robes. The offering-bowls are of a pattern you would have chosen. A priest at the door glances at you, at the lintel, at you again, as if awaiting a word.

choices.text: Stand where the pilgrims stand, and light a stick

effects.log: The stick catches. The priest watches the smoke lean toward you, and says nothing at all.

choices.text: Ask the priest how many seasons the temple has stood

effects.log: He tells you, and adds three small stories you did not ask for. One of them you already knew.

events.text: A hymn of your pantheon has a stanza you did not teach it. It tells of {llg_who} and the founding of a council, and it is sung at the great feasts of {llg_region}. You know the next line before the chorus reaches it, and you know it is a little wrong.

choices.text: Sing the true line, softly, under the choir

effects.log: The choir catches your line and, after a beat, takes it up. The cantor's face is a study.

choices.text: Let the stanza run on, and hold your tongue

effects.log: The hymn ends. It is a lovely thing, even wrong, and you carry the wrong line home like a small stone.

events.text: A sealed shrine stands in {llg_region}: {llg_thing}. No one will tell you why it is shut, though everyone knows. Your feet know the steps all the same, and your hand finds the bolt in the dark. A chill sits in your chest, as if you were the one who had to close it.

choices.text: Ask the nearest villager who still remembers it

effects.log: A woman wipes her hands on her apron and tells you, haltingly. She does not look at your face. When she finishes, she is crying.

choices.text: Walk back from the door and breathe

effects.log: You walk back, step by step, as one walks back from a ledge. The chill stays with you for a day.

events.text: {llg_Thing} is kept clear by common consent. Moss grows around it and not on it. War-gods who pass it bow stiffly and take the long way. Your own steps carry you across it before you know it, and when you look back, you see the moss has opened a path for you.

choices.text: Stop in the middle and stand still

effects.log: The wind drops. You stand in the quiet with a heaviness you cannot name, and the moss stays still around your feet.

choices.text: Cross it quickly and do not look behind

effects.log: You cross. A cold thread follows you to the far side, and loosens, slowly, over the miles.

events.text: In {llg_region}, everyone avoids a certain bend of the temple stair, and nobody can say why. You find your eyes lowering before you reach it. Under your sleeve your wrist tingles, as if the sleeve had once been tied with a cord that has long since been cut.

choices.text: Keep your eyes up and look at the bend

effects.log: The bend is a plain turn in the stone. There is a faint mark in the wall, at the height of a hand, and your own hand rises to it and stops.

choices.text: Lower your eyes with the rest of the pilgrims

effects.log: You lower your eyes. The stair is silent. You go down it the faster for it.

events.text: You have climbed this step before, though not in this shape. {llg_Thing} is smaller than you remember, or you larger, and the incense is of another kind. A young priest looks at you, then at the lintel, then at you, with the face of someone who has just recalled a name.

choices.text: Ask the priest what they remember

effects.log: The priest stammers. They remember a story, told by a grandmother, of a visitor who stood just so. They colour to the ears.

choices.text: Light a stick and say nothing

effects.log: The stick burns clean. The priest bows low, and leaves you to it, and the temple settles around you like a coat.

events.text: The drill-court in {llg_region} has new flagstones laid over the old, and somewhere beneath them, you feel, your own footprints. A young war-god, mid-form, glances up, falters, and then recovers with a bow. You find that you are standing in the stance the court was built for.

choices.text: Hold the stance until the young god finishes the form

effects.log: You hold it. The young god completes the form, shakily. The old stones, under the new, seem to take a slow breath.

choices.text: Walk the edge of the court and leave the practice to them

effects.log: You walk the edge. At the far corner a stone is warmer than the rest, and you let your hand rest on it a moment.

events.text: Someone has quietly kept {llg_thing} in good repair while you were gone: a new rail at the slippery step, fresh tiles on the north roof, a tiny mark carved under an eave that only one hand would make. The accounts say an unnamed donor has paid for it, and you recognise the hand.

choices.text: Let everything stand as it is, and leave a quiet blessing

effects.log: The tiles shine in the evening light. A sparrow lands on the rail and flies off again. The temple feels mended in more than the roof.

choices.text: Mend the one flaw you left unmended the first time

effects.log: You fix a loose beam under the eave. It takes an afternoon. The beam holds, and you wipe your hands with satisfaction.

events.text: You have stood here before. {llg_Thing} is smaller, or you larger, and the beings who keep their eyes lowered are not the same ones, but the weight is. A cold passes through you. This is the place where you did what you did, and the stones remember it, plainly, like a hand on a shoulder.

choices.text: Stay, and let the weight of it rest on you

effects.log: You stay. The cold deepens, and then steadies. A lamp somewhere is lit. You do not know if it is for you.

choices.text: Leave quietly, and come back with a plan

effects.log: You leave by the lesser gate. The stones watch you go, and the plan is already forming as you walk.

events.text: You stand on the high place when it comes to you whole. This was your peak. You named it from a cloud-saddle on a morning with a cold in your head. {llg_name}: you lived {llg_age} years, died of {llg_cause}, and now the pilgrims climb under your title and do not know whose it was.

choices.text: Plant a small marker and tend it in secret

effects.log: The marker is a stone, unlettered. You tend it each season, and no one asks who has come.

choices.text: Tell the next pilgrim at the cairn who you are

effects.log: The pilgrim, wide-eyed, laughs, then stops. He looks at the cairn and bows. The story will be in the valley by morning.

choices.text: Go down to the map-hall and correct the name

effects.log: The clerk takes your correction with scepticism and a very sharp pencil. By the next season the maps are right.

choices.text: Give toward a proper beacon for the summit

effects.log: The beacon is raised. On the first night it is lit, the pilgrims below cheer, and you stand among them, unknown.

events.text: The tale of {llg_who} is yours; it was sung about you. {llg_name}: {llg_age} years, a death of {llg_cause}, and a hymn that got half of it wrong in lovely ways. You hear a young pilgrim begin the third night, and mouth the words along with her, and know them better than she does.

choices.text: Sit at the back and let the tale be sung

effects.log: You sit. The tale goes on. You find that you like it, even in the wrong places, and that the wrongness is a kind of love.

choices.text: Stand at the end and name yourself

effects.log: The hall falls silent. The pilgrim stares. Someone laughs, nervously, and someone else kneels.

choices.text: Take the pilgrim aside and correct the verses

effects.log: She listens with her mouth open, then writes down every line with shaking fingers.

choices.text: Pay for the true tale to be cut on a stone tablet

effects.log: The tablet is cut and set in the harbour hall. The pilgrims pass it, in rows, and touch the stone with respect.

events.text: The barren rise in {llg_region} is your work. It returns to you now whole: the days before it, and the choice. {llg_name}: {llg_age} years, ending in {llg_cause}, leaving a hill that no pilgrim climbs. You stand at its rim in the thin air, and it feels your weight.

choices.text: Look for the families who remain and do what you can for them

effects.log: A family in the valley, the third you ask, takes you in. They do not know you. They set a bowl before you, and it is heavy to hold.

choices.text: Clear away whatever is left standing there

effects.log: You clear it, piece by piece, over a season. At the end the rise is only a rise, and the wind crosses it freely.

choices.text: Tell the pilgrims plainly who you were

effects.log: You tell them. They listen, white-faced. One of them spits. One of them stays to hear it to the end.

choices.text: Have the whole account written down, without softening

effects.log: The account is written by a scribe who stops twice to wipe her eyes. It is entered in the Book of Fates under a number, and anyone may find it.

events.text: The grim tale of {llg_who} is yours. The tellers soften its worst chapter, and you remember that chapter exactly. {llg_name}: {llg_age} years, a death by {llg_cause}. Every telling paints a monster, and you cannot honestly say the portrait is false.

choices.text: Seek out the descendants and sit with them

effects.log: You find them, in a hill village. They do not turn you away. They do not forgive you either, and the not-forgiving is its own kind of welcome.

choices.text: Gather every copy of the tale you can find and put it to the fire

effects.log: The pyre is small. The tale, you find, does not burn. It lives in the mouths of the hill-folk, as before.

choices.text: Tell them to their faces who you were

effects.log: You say it. A woman rises and leaves the room. A man nods, slowly, as if he had been expecting you for years.

choices.text: Have the true account set down in full

effects.log: The account runs to a hundred pages. The clerk reads it twice and asks if you want the worst part left in. You do.

events.text: You tend {llg_thing} the way it ought to be tended. Nobody asks who you are. Lamps trimmed, stairs swept, incense kept dry. Slowly the faithful notice that someone has been careful with the place. An old nun leaves a gift of tea at the door each dawn and does not wait to be thanked.

choices.text: Keep it up, season on season

effects.log: The seasons wheel. The tea arrives each dawn. You find that you are, without choosing it, part of the place.

choices.text: Teach a young keeper the work

effects.log: The young keeper is clumsy and eager. By spring the stair is swept in half the time, and the lamps are never allowed to gutter.

events.text: You tend the dark thing as one tends a grave: carefully, daily, without ceremony. The court watches, uncertain whether it is penance or presumption. After a season someone leaves a lamp at the gate. After a year, two. The lamps go on burning, and nobody speaks of them.

choices.text: Keep on, however slowly forgiveness comes

effects.log: You keep on. The lamps accumulate at the gate, one by one, like small clean stars.

choices.text: Ask a survivor what they would have you do

effects.log: She names three things, plain and hard. You do all three, and she does not thank you, and that is right.

events.text: You told them. Some here are the grandchildren of those who knew {llg_who}, and they have a test ready, since you are not the first to say it: three questions. What did {llg_he} eat at dawn? Whom did {llg_he} never forgive? What carried {llg_he} off? A hush fills the court. No claimant has ever answered all three.

choices.text: Answer as only you could

ok.log: You answer all three without hesitation. The eldest sits back slowly. One by one, the others bow.

fail.log: You falter on the second. They smile politely, and the heads shake.

choices.text: Show them a piece of the old skill

ok.log: The old stance comes into your body unbidden. The challenger yields. It is exactly the stance in the old carving.

fail.log: The challenger is faster than the carving implied. You go down, and the doubters nod.

choices.text: Laugh, and say it was only a jest

effects.log: They laugh with you, relieved. The question stays in the court like a feather in the air.

events.text: You told them who you were. Nobody forgave anything. They listened as one listens to a verdict, and some rose to leave and then did not. The silence afterward was the longest of your existence, and the lamps in the hall went on burning.

choices.text: Stand there and take whatever comes

effects.log: Nothing comes. The silence stays. Then someone, somewhere, begins to weep quietly, and another voice joins her.

choices.text: Offer to go, and stay only if they say stay

effects.log: No one says stay. No one says go. You stand in the door, and at last the old woman beckons you to a seat.

events.text: The tale of {llg_who} has grown wrong in a hundred ways and right in a few. You go from pilgrim to pilgrim, correcting small things, patiently: the date, the ending, the soup. One resists, then softens. "It is a worse tale," she says, "and truer. I will sing the true one at the steps."

choices.text: Give her the true verses one by one

effects.log: She writes them down. She sings them at the steps that night, and the crowd goes quiet at the third line.

choices.text: Leave her to decide which tale to keep

effects.log: She decides slowly. In the morning she is still humming something you do not recognise, and perhaps it is hers.

events.text: You have written the whole of it down, the worst included. The Book of Fates reads it twice and asks if it should be entered under your name. You hesitate. The clerk nods, understanding, and offers a number instead. The entry is open to any scholar who cares to look.

choices.text: Sign it, at last, with your old name

effects.log: You sign. The brush shakes once. The clerk blows on the ink, and says nothing, and the room is very still.

choices.text: Leave it unsigned, under the number

effects.log: The number is stamped. You walk out of the record hall into a thin evening light, and the weight is a little lighter and a little different.

events.text: The work goes on all year: the drain they ought to have dug, the broken step, the roof. The chief mason asks whose offerings these are. Nobody's, you say. He looks at your plans, then at the old wall, then at you. "Same hand," he mutters, and decides it is none of his business. At the end the temple holds a feast for the unnamed donor, and you sit at the foot of the table.

choices.text: Attend the feast and eat heartily

effects.log: You eat three helpings. The mason raises a cup in your direction without a word.

choices.text: Scratch a small mark on a beam where only you would look

effects.log: The mark is a tiny crooked bird. Years from now someone will find it, and wonder.

events.text: A roofed hall goes up beside the old drill-court, a place to rest between forms and to practise out of the rain. The war-gods who use it call the donor "the Dry One," and bless the name each wet morning. You smile at it and let it stand.

choices.text: Sit in the hall on a rainy day, among strangers
